dataset_name: High Mountain Asia Glacial Lake Outburst Flood Database (HMAGLOFDB)

temporal_qc_audit.maintainer_documentation_notice: The database has been quality controlled up to 2025/12/31. Events with a later date in the database need to be evaluated and cross checked.
temporal_qc_audit.policy: Original raw records preserved untouched without silent modification. Unverified post-2025 events and pre-instrumental documentary accounts flagged for explicit QC.

plus_counts_audit.interpretation: Values formatted as '+' represent positive-but-unknown counts and must never be converted to zero.

blockers: HMAGLOFDB is an event-only inventory (774 positive events); no verified non-event observations exist.
Unrecorded lake-years in GLO cannot be assumed to be true negatives without historical observation bias.
Pre-event lake area is missing in 95.1% of recorded events.
Overall impact narrative is available for only 3.6% of events (28 / 774).
Casualties (Lives_total) recorded for only 4.1% of events; missing reports cannot be assumed to equal 0.
Infrastructure damage recorded for only 11.4% of events.
Grouping narrative text into 'LOW / MEDIUM / HIGH' creates arbitrary, uncalibrated subjective targets.
Crucial physical outcomes (discharge, casualties, mechanism) are post-event leakage, not pre-event features.

feasibility_gate.rationale: Model training is strictly NO-GO for both GLOF occurrence and GLOF impact severity. HMAGLOFDB provides invaluable historical geomorphological reference context, but its extreme missingness (>87% across damage fields), event-only nature, and post-event character of documented mechanisms prevent training a defensible, reproducible machine learning classifier. GlacierGuard-AI must maintain GLOF hazard assessment as a rule-based expert glaciological surveillance tier, distinct from the validated annual lake area change regression tier.
